key_insight: Support-constrained offline reinforcement learning improves estimated pediatric ECMO decision quality while staying closer to clinician actions than standard Fitted Q-Iteration.
engineering_relevance: Restricting optimization to data-supported actions and using a clinician baseline in sparse regions offers a practical safeguard for learning from limited clinical data.
method: Train Support-Constrained Fitted Q-Iteration (FQI-SC) on offline clinical trajectories.
Optimize only over empirically supported state-action pairs; default to the clinician baseline in low-data regions.
Assess estimated value, clinician-action disagreement, and a unified performance-safety Balance Score.
evidence_signal: On 78 pediatric trajectories spanning over 6,000 clinical hours, FQI-SC achieved a 38% higher Balance Score and 71% lower clinician-action disagreement than FQI, plus 1.28 higher FQE-estimated value than imitation learning.
watch_item: Offline value estimates and clinician agreement do not establish clinical safety or reduced neurological injury; prospective validation is needed.
paper_title: Support-Constrained Offline Policy Improvement for Pediatric ECMO from Limited Clinical Data
